title: Python SDK: unified hydrator & representation layer for streaming + typed models
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a unified 'Hydrator & Representation' layer for the Python SDK that: 1) accepts raw streaming events (chunked JSON + token deltas) and reliably assembles typed response objects, 2) interoperates with both dataclass and pydantic user types, 3) supports backpressure-friendly async iteration and checkpointed hydration for retries and reconnects, and 4) minimizes allocations for high-throughput hosted workloads. This ticket covers API design, a lightweight adapter registry, core streaming parser integration, perf microbenchmarks, tests, and docs/examples.
acceptance_criteria: Hydrator API present as sdk.hydrators.unified.Hydrator with methods: from_stream(async_iterator), from_payload(dict)
Hydrator supports three representation modes via adapter registry: 'dataclass', 'pydantic', and 'plain-dict'
Streaming hydrate path yields an async iterator of model instances and preserves ordering and partial-output markers
Reconnect/retry semantics: hydrator can resume from a token/kv checkpoint without duplicating emitted model instances
Unit + integration tests cover streaming parse, model conversion, error handling, and memory regression tests
Documentation and two example notebooks demonstrating dataclass-first and pydantic-first workflows
design_decisions: Adapter registry instead of single canonical representation: avoids forcing customers into dataclass or pydantic and keeps runtime small

Streaming-first API: prioritize an async iterator that emits hydrated models as soon as full semantic units are available (e.g., a single message or command), rather than waiting for the entire response
Shallow-copy semantics for hydrate_from_chunk: avoid deep copies where possible, prefer views and lightweight wrappers to reduce GC pressure
Opt out of automatic validation for high-throughput mode; provide an explicit .validate() hook to allow customers to check models post-hydration
Retry semantics use idempotent checkpoints (token_index, kv_entries_hash) stored alongside iterator state for resume
technical_notes: Core parser will reuse existing streaming JSON tokenizer implemented in sdk.parsers.stream_json to assemble partial objects
Hydrator will expose two entry points: Hydrator.from_stream(async_iter[bytes|str|dict]) -> AsyncIterator[Model] and Hydrator.from_payload(dict) -> Model
Adapter interface: class AdapterProtocol: to_model(payload: dict) -> Any; adapters registered with @register_adapter('pydantic') etc.
Performance target: keep per-token overhead <= 20% added latency compared to raw string stream parsing for typical chat responses (seq len 512) on c5-style worker in benchmark harness
Implementation plan: iterate with feature flag 'hydrator-unified' behind sdk feature flags; land minimal adapter + tests, then add pydantic and dataclass wrappers in follow-ups
Telemetry: emit meter 'sdk.hydrator.latency' and counter 'sdk.hydrator.errors' to console metrics for rollout monitoring
Compatibility: maintain backward-compatible API for sync helpers used in existing examples (provide sync wrapper that consumes the async iterator)

We will not attempt zero-copy into user pydantic models (impractical due to dataclass/pydantic constructors), but will minimize intermediate allocations by parsing to dicts and streaming those to adapter constructors

implementation_notes: Prototype settled on registry API to avoid heavy coupling: register_adapter(name: str, adapter_cls)
We implemented short-circuit for plain-dict adapter which returns the parsed payload directly when users request 'plain-dict' mode
Added explicit error class HydrationError with codes: PARSE_FAIL, ADAPTER_FAIL, CHECKPOINT_MISMATCH
Hydrator supports optional schema coercion hook for minor type fixes (string->int, iso8601->datetime) configurable per-adapter
Initial microbenchmarks: end-to-end streaming hydrate on 10k small messages achieved 15% overhead versus raw parse baseline on dev box; need a run on CI runners and dedicated throughput nodes
Memory leak: observed retained payloads when using pydantic v1 in repeated hydrate runs; mitigation: use temporary weakrefs and explicit del in adapter, tracked in ENG-199001
notes_on_tradeoffs: Decision to not force validation by default keeps common happy path fast but shifts responsibility to users wanting strictness
Adapter registry adds complexity but reduces friction for customers using different model systems; alternative (single canonical model) was rejected to protect ergonomics
We accept small extra allocations for pydantic due to constructor semantics; future work could explore pydantic-core integration once stable in our supported Python versions
